div.p: Worked through a,b,c, with b hidden and c sorted descending. Every stage names its columns by position.

The carried columns: everything on display, then any column a sort key or a filter names, by their file positions. This is where a hidden column drops out, and where the columns take the order the user put them in.
Prepends the row id, the row's position in the file, which it keeps through every later stage.
The shape is now fixed. The row id is at 0 and each carried column is at its place in the carried list, and every stage below reads those same numbers.
Runs once the user has filtered. One moonblade expression, the filters ANDed, written by expression.lua and addressing columns as col(2).
This stage and the select and enum above it are narrowing_stages. count, stats and frequency open their own pipelines with the same three, so they report on the rows the user is looking at.
One stage per key, least significant first, because xan sort applies one direction to all its keys and is stable. -N numeric, -R descending.
The page. Everything above decides which rows exist. Everything below is presentation.
The row id, then one clause per displayed column: the printf spec or the detected decimal count, padding to the width the user pinned, a trailing space, and the header text to draw it under.

Column widths are applied here. Every cell in a pinned column leaves at exactly that width, cut with an ellipsis if it ran long. The header is cut to the same width, because view sizes a column to its widest cell and the header is one of the cells.
try wraps anything that can fail, so a value that fails to cast falls back to its raw text.
-e draws every column at the width its content already has, which is the width the clause above gave it. Left to itself, view fits the table to the terminal.
-A every row, -M -I drop the meta rows, -r right-aligns the numeric columns by position.

Reads the row ids out of the first cell, then cuts that cell from every line. The border lines reach the buffer with the rest, so the table keeps its frame, and statuscolumn.lua draws the row number in the gutter.
